candidate.summary:
WORKING PROPOSAL, not canon. No accepted Identity and no declared architecture preference exist, so the causal organization here is an agent proposal: a primary engine with subordinate layers. A single center would be too narrow for twelve Books of generational time; an ensemble would diffuse the one question the series is built to keep open.

The primary engine is The Irreversible Copy. Authority is extended before it can be verified, and once extended the book is copied, distributed, and cannot be recalled, so the consequence of a reception always arrives in the hands of someone who did not decide. Six subordinate engines are not decorations on that engine; they are the specific reasons it cannot be settled. Inherited Warrant makes each generation the receiver of its ancestors, so anonymity is a phase of transmission rather than an exception inside it. The Displacement Ledger prices every yes in uncopied books. Reading as the Only Verification makes taste the instrument of authority, and taste is formed by the archive it is judging. Faithful Contradiction makes a received text permanently incompatible with the corpus while forbidding repair. Instrumental Demand makes unattributable texts valuable to the powerful precisely because no author can be held to them. Proxy Attribution settles the cost on whoever last handled the book.

The emotional promise is a compound held as co-primary: earned trust, stated by the author, and the dread of the unchecked, proposed here. Trust that has never been afraid of being wrong is flattery, so fear is load-bearing rather than atmospheric. The complex emotion the series is finally after is Trust That Has a Receipt.

Genres are working hypotheses, since the vision names none: institutional chronicle governing; novel of ideas, epistemic suspense, generational succession, and institutional comedy supporting; archival form tertiary.

Twelve phases trace one arc: an extension that is unrecorded, then costed, then contradictory, then blamed, then instrumental, then inherited, then refused to the point of starvation, then recorded, then contested, then reified, then handed over, then closed by choice. The invented pivot is the wager record: a reception dated, signed, and given a condition under which it should be reopened. It is not a cure. The record is copied, and the next generation trusts the record without its reasons, which restarts the engine one level up. That recursion is what keeps the ending an act instead of an answer, and what lets anonymity stay neither fatal nor set aside.

nodes.title: The Irreversible Copy
nodes.summary: The primary engine. A book's authority can only be extended by receiving it into the copying queue, and reception cannot be undone: the copy is made, distributed, and outlives its copyist. Verification of an anonymous text is structurally late, so it can only arrive as consequences felt by people who did not make the decision. The recurring pressure is that the monastery must act on a judgment it cannot discharge, and every act of generosity also commits the institution's name. Actors under this engine do not choose between a right and a wrong answer; they choose between two ways of being wrong, one discoverable inside a lifetime and one not.

nodes.title: Inherited Warrant
nodes.summary: Each generation inherits its predecessors' receptions as settled fact, stripped of the reading that justified them. This converts the primary engine from a repeated event into an accumulating structure: the monks are not only deciding about anonymous authors, they are the anonymous authors of their own tradition's warrants. Its action pattern is re-reading under a closed door - someone tries to recover why a text was admitted and finds only the admission. Its pressure is arithmetic: the archive's authority grows by exactly the amount of reasoning it has lost.

nodes.title: The Displacement Ledger
nodes.summary: Copying is slow, and shelf and scribal hours are finite, so every reception is also a refusal of something else. This engine makes generosity cost something the reader can count. Its action pattern is arithmetic performed under moral pressure: which unadmitted book loses its place because this one was taken. Its pressure is that the monastery can never know the value of what it displaced, because the counterfactual book is not in the archive to be read. This is the engine that forbids the series from concluding that openness is simply better.

nodes.title: Reading as the Only Verification
nodes.summary: With provenance unavailable, the only remaining test of an anonymous book is whether it coheres with the received corpus, answers questions its readers actually bring, and survives repeated use. That makes taste the instrument of authority, and taste is trained by the same corpus it is judging. The action pattern is comparison under uncertainty: this passage sounds like us, this one does not, and the ear making the judgment was formed by the archive under judgment. Its pressure is a circularity that cannot be escaped, only made visible - which is also the engine's gift, since visible circularity can be owned.

nodes.title: Faithful Contradiction
nodes.summary: The monastery's fidelity rule is absolute: a copied text is transmitted as received, never emended. So a received book that contradicts the corpus must either be carried as a permanent contradiction or refused entirely. This generates the sharpest recurring crisis of the horizon, and it recurs without repeating because the content of each contradiction differs while the rule that forbids repair never does. The action pattern is the search for an honest third option that does not exist - annotation, quarantine, separate shelving - each of which turns out to be either a refusal or an emendation wearing a procedure.

nodes.title: The Instrumental Orphan
nodes.summary: The archive has clients outside it: those who need legitimation, those who need precedent, those who need a mistake they can point at. An unattributable text serves all three, because no author can be punished, contradicted, or asked to recant. This supplies the external pressure that makes the central question urgent rather than scholarly, and it does so without requiring a villain, since every client's interest is individually defensible. The action pattern is the persuasive offer - admit this, for a reason that is genuinely good and happens to serve us.

nodes.title: Proxy Attribution
nodes.summary: When no author exists, responsibility migrates to the transmitter. This produces the recurring social crisis: someone is held to account for a sentence they transcribed and did not write, and the account is procedurally correct. The action pattern is the search for a stand-in - the copyist, the receiving house, the last named commentator - followed by the discovery that the stand-in is the only party who can in fact be held. This is where the series shows what a name is for: not proof of truth, but a place to put the cost.

nodes.title: The Wager Architecture
nodes.summary: The repeating rhythmic unit every Book of the horizon shares without repeating its content: a reception crisis appears; available verification is structurally insufficient; a decision is made that cannot be recalled; the consequence arrives a generation later, in the hands of someone who did not decide. The unit's force comes from the temporal offset, since decision and cost always sit in different Books, so the reader learns to read every reception as a debt. It is deliberately not a plot template: it specifies what kind of pressure must exist, never what happens.

nodes.title: The Two Ledgers
nodes.summary: Every Book keeps two accounts and teaches the reader to read both: what was received and on what grounds, and what was refused and what the refusal cost. The second ledger is the series' conscience and its most fragile structure, because refusals leave no copies to consult - they survive only as entries. When someone later asks what the archive would look like had a refusal gone the other way, the answer exists only there. The ledger is also the first thing an institution stops maintaining when it is frightened, which makes its condition a running index of the monastery's honesty.

nodes.title: The Starvation Line
nodes.summary: A subordinate line running the full horizon. Want: an archive open enough to keep answering the questions its readers bring. Resistance: the fear of contamination, which is always locally reasonable and never absurd. Change: strictness is repeatedly proven costly in concrete, unfixable ways, so the line moves from an argument about safety to an argument about what a tradition is for. This is the line that makes the extension necessary rather than merely kind, because it shows what a closed archive loses and who pays for the loss.

nodes.title: The Accountability Line
nodes.summary: Want: a responsible party for every text, so that being wrong has somewhere to land. Resistance: structural anonymity, which no amount of diligence removes. Change: the line stops hunting an author and starts constructing a receiver, ending not in a recovered identity but in a documented, dated, contestable act of reception. This line carries the series' answer to the danger, and that answer is deliberately procedural rather than metaphysical - it is about who owns a judgment, not about what is true.

nodes.title: The Coherence Line
nodes.summary: Want: a corpus that holds together well enough to be used, taught, and argued from. Resistance: faithful contradiction, which the fidelity rule forbids resolving by repair. Change: coherence is demoted across the horizon from a gate that decides admission to a stated cost a reception accepts. This is where the series does its most technical work, because it must show a tradition remaining usable while inconsistent, without pretending the inconsistency is a richness or a secret harmony.

nodes.title: The Succession Line
nodes.summary: Want: to hand on something intact. Resistance: reasons decay faster than texts, so what is handed on is always less than what was meant. Change: the line moves from preserving the archive, to choosing what to hand on, to handing on the practice of re-deciding rather than the decisions themselves. This converts inheritance from a setting detail into the series' central action, and it is the mechanism that lets the horizon end by choice rather than by depletion.

nodes.title: Authority Is Extended, Not Possessed
nodes.summary: Authority is not a property a text carries but an act a receiver performs: the monastery does not find authority in a book, it confers it, and the conferral is what makes the book citable as tradition. This reverses the usual direction of the problem. The corruption the series must fear is not in the anonymous author alone but in the receiver's capacity to be wrong, and the receiver is the party the reader can actually watch. The theme forbids every consolation in which a sufficiently careful reading recovers the missing guarantee.

nodes.title: Anonymity Transfers Risk to the Receiver
nodes.summary: Anonymity does not erase responsibility; it relocates its cost forward in time, onto every reader who must act without a guarantor. The unnamed author has offloaded the labour of verification onto strangers who cannot reach them. This reading keeps the danger specific and keeps anonymity from becoming a neutral technical condition, because something is genuinely taken from the receiver in the transaction: recourse. It also keeps the necessity specific, since the same transaction is what lets a text travel when its author cannot.

nodes.title: A Name Is Leverage, Not Truth
nodes.summary: What a name buys is not proof but contestability: someone to argue with, someone to credit, someone to refuse. Precision about this is what allows the series to hold its two commitments at once. Anonymity is not fatal, because a text without an author can still be received well. Anonymity is not irrelevant, because a text without an author cannot be contested at its source, and the argument must therefore be had with the transmitter instead. The theme gives the series a precise vocabulary for loss without converting loss into doom.

nodes.title: Incomplete Knowledge Is the Working Condition
nodes.summary: Incompleteness is not an obstacle the monastery will eventually clear; it is the medium in which all its judgment occurs. The theme is stated structurally rather than morally: the archive is incomplete, the record is incomplete, and the reader's knowledge is incomplete in exactly the same way and for the same reason. That symmetry is the series' ethical engine, because it makes the reader a participant in the wager rather than an auditor of it, and it forbids any ending in which completeness arrives and settles the question.

nodes.title: Endings Are Chosen, Never Exhausted
nodes.summary: A conclusion is legitimate because someone with standing chose it, dated it, and left it reopenable - not because the material ran out. This theme supplies the series' only honest form of closure, since its central question cannot be answered without violating its premise. Closure becomes an act of custody: the monastery closes a period of discernment rather than declaring the matter settled, and the reader is asked to accept that act as sufficient instead of accepting a proof.

nodes.title: The Unverifiable Warrant
nodes.summary: A claim whose backing is structurally unavailable, used anyway, so that every use is a wager. At scene scale this is the primary engine's basic unit: a text is cited in a way that matters before anything about it can be checked. The trope's discipline is that the missing backing must be shown to be missing for a reason, not merely withheld by the author for suspense.

nodes.title: The Costing Yes
nodes.summary: Every inclusion is a visible exclusion. The trope forces an admission to be shown together with the specific uncopied thing it displaced, so generosity is never permitted to be costless on the page. Its strength is that it makes the reader complicit in the arithmetic: by the middle of the horizon the reader has preferences among the refused books and knows those preferences were formed without reading them.

nodes.title: The Inherited Verdict
nodes.summary: A decision outlives its reasons and is obeyed as though the reasons still held. The trope recurs because institutions store conclusions and discard arguments, and because the discarded argument is usually the only thing that could have revised the conclusion. Its payoff shape is the moment a living person discovers they are enforcing a dead person's judgment about a world that no longer exists - and that the dead person may have been right.

nodes.title: The Trained Ear
nodes.summary: A judgment of authenticity made by someone whose sense of authenticity was formed by the thing being judged. The trope prevents the series from offering connoisseurship as a substitute for provenance. It recurs in the form of an expert who is right for reasons they cannot defend and wrong for reasons they cannot see, and it is the engine of the reader's own discomfort, since the reader's ear is being trained by the series at the same time.

nodes.title: The Faithful Contradiction
nodes.summary: Fidelity requires transmitting something that damages the whole. The trope is the series' sharpest pressure device because it offers no correct option: refuse and lose a true thing, copy and carry a permanent injury, emend and commit the one act the institution regards as unforgivable. It recurs with different content and the same shape, and its accumulation across the horizon is what finally makes coherence a cost rather than a gate.

nodes.title: The Useful Orphan
nodes.summary: An unattributable thing is valuable precisely because no one can be held to it. The trope turns the archive's problem into other people's instrument, so that the monks' dilemma acquires clients, leverage, and urgency. Its discipline is refusing villainy: the party making the offer should be right on the merits and wrong in the aggregate, which is the most uncomfortable and most truthful shape available.

nodes.title: The Proxy Accused
nodes.summary: Blame migrates to whoever handled the thing last, and the migration is procedurally correct. The trope is where the series' comedy and its cruelty share a single mechanism, because an absurd assignment of blame is also a defensible one. Its payoff is always the same recognition in a new costume: the cost of anonymity does not disappear, it simply finds a body.

nodes.title: The Record Turned Relic
nodes.summary: The corrective instrument becomes the next unread authority. The record is copied, quoted, cited, and finally trusted without its reasons, so the monastery manufactures a new anonymous book - its own. This is the series' recursive engine and its best protection against a too-tidy answer: any procedure invented to make reception accountable becomes, one generation later, an accountability it can no longer explain.

nodes.title: The Open Handing Over
nodes.summary: Succession as a choice among live options rather than a default. The trope requires at least two genuinely viable things to hand on - the decisions, the reasons, or the practice of re-deciding - and requires the choice to cost something the chooser valued. It is the trope that makes the required ending possible, because it locates closure in an act of custody rather than in the exhaustion of material.

nodes.title: Institutional Chronicle
nodes.summary: The governing genre, proposed rather than declared. Its subject is the institution across periods long enough that no single person spans the consequence of their own decision. Its pleasures are structural: accumulated consequence, procedure under strain, and the slow revelation that an organization's character is the residue of its unexamined rulings. It is chosen because the vision's question is asked generation after generation, which only an institutional timescale can make into pressure rather than theme.

nodes.title: Novel of Ideas
nodes.summary: A supporting genre, proposed. Its contribution is that argument becomes action: a proposition is tested by whether the institution will act on it before it is settled, not by whether it is elegantly stated. The genre is kept subordinate deliberately, because a novel of ideas that governs would let the series debate its central question instead of paying for it, and the vision requires the extension to be felt as dangerous rather than discussed as difficult.

nodes.title: Epistemic Suspense
nodes.summary: A supporting genre, proposed. Suspense is generated by the shape of the institution's knowledge rather than by threat: verification is always available in principle and never available in time. This genre is what converts unverifiability from a premise into a feeling, and it is the main reason fear can carry a primary emotional role without the series becoming a thriller.

nodes.title: Generational Succession Narrative
nodes.summary: A supporting genre, proposed. It supplies the body that ages: handoffs, inherited obligations, and the specific grief of receiving something from someone whose intentions are no longer recoverable. Used here without a continuous cast, so attachment attaches to the office, the archive, and the ledger rather than to persons - a choice that intensifies the theme at the cost of some conventional reader intimacy.

nodes.title: Institutional Comedy
nodes.summary: A supporting genre, proposed, and the series' most necessary corrective. Comedy keeps trust from hardening into reverence by exposing that much of the dread is produced by procedure rather than danger. Its function is not relief but critique: the absurdity it reveals is load-bearing, and the laughter stops at the exact moment a ruling becomes a penalty. Without it, twelve Books of grave discernment would teach the reader to be solemn about the question instead of honest about it.

nodes.title: Archival Form
nodes.summary: A tertiary genre, proposed. The series is built partly from apparatus: catalogue entries, reception notes, refusals, marginal disputes, later hands annotating earlier ones. The form performs the theme instead of illustrating it, because the reader receives the institution's reasoning in the same degraded state the monks do. Its danger is distance, so it is held tertiary and never allowed to become the primary surface.

nodes.title: The Plain Hand
nodes.summary: Prose that reads like good copying: unadorned, exact, slightly worn, with visible seams where a later hand has intervened. Sentences are built to be transmitted rather than admired, and the few moments of figurative writing carry disproportionate weight because the surface has earned them. The strategy makes fidelity perceptible as a texture, so the reader can feel the difference between a line that was copied and a line that was mended.

nodes.title: Catalogue and Marginalia
nodes.summary: The series' apparatus is not decoration but a second narrative surface. Catalogue entries record what exists; the two ledgers record what was decided and what it cost; marginalia carry opinions the main text will not state. Quoted without editorial gloss, the apparatus lets the reader do the interpretive work the institution refuses to do, which is also how the reader is recruited into the wager.

nodes.title: Withheld Light
nodes.summary: Tension is produced by what is not shown rather than by what threatens. Provenance is withheld without narratorial comment; periods end at the moment of commitment rather than at the moment of discovery; the reader is allowed to notice the gap before any character names it. The calibration rule is strict: nothing is withheld that a reader could not reasonably be expected to miss, so the eventual noticing feels like attention rewarded rather than a trick revealed.

nodes.title: Comic Deflation
nodes.summary: Sudden registers of institutional absurdity placed exactly where the series risks self-importance. The comedy is deadpan and never winks; the funniest line in a period should be a correct ruling. Deflation is used as an instrument of critique, and it is withdrawn at the moment a consequence becomes personal, so that the reader experiences the withdrawal as the removal of a protection they had been enjoying.

nodes.title: Dated Voice
nodes.summary: Each generation's idiom is distinct enough that the reader can feel the drift of vocabulary while the argument stays the same. This is the aesthetic instrument of the Inherited Warrant engine: when the words change and the conclusion does not, the reader sees that the conclusion has become a relic while everyone inside the period experiences it as agreement. Voice drift is tracked deliberately across the horizon and never explained by a narrator.

nodes.title: Earned Trust
nodes.summary: The governing promise, named by the author. The reader should finish each Book with confidence in the monastery's judgment that is proportional to what the Book showed it costing, and finish the horizon with a trust that knows its own terms. Earned is the operative word: the experience must be distinguishable from the comfort of a tradition that has never been tested, and a reader who has not been made afraid somewhere in the horizon should not be able to feel it at all.

nodes.title: The Dread of the Unchecked
nodes.summary: A steady, low-grade unease that what the reader has accepted as true was accepted on someone's word, and that the word cannot now be checked. The dread is directed at the reading experience itself rather than at any threat inside the story, which is what makes it survive the absence of a villain. It must be sustained long enough to become familiar, since the series' payoff depends on the reader recognizing the feeling as their own condition rather than a character's predicament.

nodes.title: Reader Complicity
nodes.summary: The reader is a receiver too. They cannot verify the texts either, they form preferences among the refused books without reading them, and they judge receptions they could not have made better. The series uses apparatus and temporal offset to make this structural rather than rhetorical: the reader is never told they are implicated, they are simply placed where the monks stand and left to notice. This is the experience that converts the theme from a claim about monks into a claim about reading.

nodes.title: The Relief of Custody
nodes.summary: The warmth of a chain of hands: the felt security of being one link among many, holding something one did not choose and did not make. This is the series' counterweight to dread, and it is deliberately not optimism about outcomes - it is the pleasure of belonging to a practice. It has to remain available even in the darkest periods, because the required ending depends on the reader accepting custody, rather than certainty, as a sufficient form of closure.
